Petitioners have filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the death of Tejas K., in the road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 19.05.2022, Tejas K., was travelling after boarded the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-6199 at Devanahalli bus stop. On the said day, at about 9-15 when the said bus was proceeding on B.B. Road and reached Agalagurkhi village gate bus stop, Chikkaballapura Taluk, Tejas was at door steps in order to get down from the bus.
At that time, the driver of the above said bus without stopping the bus suddenly moved it in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life without observing any traffic rules.
Due to the said impact, Tejas K., fell down on the road from the bus and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, Tejas K., was shifted to Ananya hospital in an Auto,
after first aid, he was referred to Government Hospital.

Due to severe head injuries sustained by Tejas K., he was referred to NIMHANS, Bengaluru in an Ambulance, but he was succumbed to injuries on the same day at about 1.00 p.m., while providing better treatment.
After postmortem, the dead body of deceased was handed over to petitioners.
Petitioners have shifted the dead body to their residence by hiring the vehicle and performed funeral and obsequies ceremony by incurring Rs.1,00,000/-.

Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy, he was completed 7th standard,
he was participated in co-curricular activities.
Due to sudden death of deceased the petitioners have lost love and affectionate and care taking son in their old age and they are undergoing deep mental shock as well as pain and suffering.

The accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-6199 by its driver and in this regard Chikkaballapura traffic police have registered the case in Cr.No.33/2022 and filed charge sheet against the driver of Krishna.T vs Manjunatha on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54824978/
2 above said vehicle.
The 1st respondent being the RC owner of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-6199 and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of above said bus and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
With these averments petitioners prays to allow the petition.
3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the respondents appeared through their counsel and the 2nd respondent has filed the written statement.
In-spite of sufficient opportunity, the 1st respondent has not filed any written statement.

4. The written statement averments of the 2 nd respondent/Insurance company are as hereunder:
The 2nd respondent has admitted that the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-016-D-6199 was insured with this respondent and contended that, the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, provisions of M.V. Act, valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of said bus, valid R.C., F.C. and permit.
Further, there is no c o m p l i a n c e o f S e c . 1 3 4 ( c ) a n d 1 5 8 ( 6 ) o f M V A c t .

T h e b u s b e a r i n g Reg.No.KA-06-D-6199 was not at all involved in the accident, the driver of said bus was not holding valid driving licence and the said bus was not having valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.
As such the owner of the said vehicle has committed the breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it has denied the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased and age of the deceased.
With these averments, the 2nd respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
:ISSUES:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Tejas K., was died in the accident occurred on 19.05.2022 at about 9.15 a.m., at Agalagurkhi village Gate Bus Stop on B.B. Road, Chikkaballapura Taluk, due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 06-D-6199 as stated in the petition?
2.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are entitled for the compensation?

If so, to what extend and from whom?
3. What order or award?

9. ISSUE No.1:-

Before going to discuss issue No.1 it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009)
13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".
Hence it is settled position of law that the petitioners have to prove their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
10. It is the case of the petitioners that, the deceased Tejas K., was travelling in the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-6199 on B.B. Road, Agalagurkhi village gate bus stop, Chikkaballapura Taluk.
At about 9-15, when the deceased Tejas K., was tried get down from the bus, the driver of said bus moved the bus in a rash or negligent manner without observing the traffic rues.
Due to which, the deceased Tejas K., fell down on the road from the bus and sustained grievous injuries.
Further, he was succumbed to injuries while taking treatment in the hospital.

12. The 2nd respondent has denied the allegations of the petition filed by the petitioner and also denied the involvement of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-6199 in the accident.
In order to substantiate the same, the 2nd respondent has examined one witness namely Likith K.E., Legal Executive as R.W.2.
R.W.2 has reiterated the written statement averments by filing affidavit in lieu of examination-in-chief.
In support of his evidence he has not produced any documents.
During the course of cross- examination R.W.2 has admitted that, they have not challenged the charge sheet filed by the police.
13. Now, the important question before this Tribunal is to find whether the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-6199 by its driver or not?
In order to answer this aspect, it is appropriate to take Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.3, Ex.P.6 to Ex.P.8.
On careful perusal of these documents, it is clear that, criminal case was registered against the driver of private Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-6199.
Apart from that, charge sheet was submitted against the driver of the above said bus for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 304(A) and also U/Sec.192 of MV Act as per Ex.P.3.

Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent driving of Bus bearing Reg.No. KA-06-D-6199 by its driver.

14. Now, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaju and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
15.

At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the deceased was got down from the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-6199, the driver of the said bus drove the same in a rash or negligent manner without following the traffic rules.
Due to the said impact, the deceased Tejas K., fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to injuries while taking treatment in the hospital.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that driver of the private Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-6199 has caused the accident.
The above referred decision is squarely applicable to the case on hand.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: This tribunal has carefully gone through the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in detail discussion regarding just compensation and also discussed regarding the criteria and formula in arriving at the conclusion to award compensation in the case of death of minor.
The Hon'ble High court of Karnataka has given the ready reckoner regarding the sums payable to the death of minor aged below 15 years in the Motors Vehicle Accident.
In the instant case both petitioners are the parents of the deceased minor.
As per the Ex.P18 the date of birth of petitioner is 26.03.2009 and the accident took place in the year 2022.
As such as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 13 years.
As per the table given by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka, Table No. 3.2 is applicable to the case on hand.

By applying the said table to the present facts of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,16,715/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
18.
Regarding liability and interest.

Driving License:- The 2nd respondent has contended that, the driver of offending Bus bearing Reg.No. KA-06-D-6199 was not holding valid driving license at the time of accident, but it has not produced the documents in order to prove the same.
Charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that the driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.

Therefore,
it appears to this Tribunal that, the driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid D.L. to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Insurance Policy, liability and Interest:-
In the instant case, respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-6199 and it was in force as on the date of accident.
The same was subject to the terms and conditions.

19. Now, Next important contention of the 2nd respondent is that the Bus bearing Reg.No.
KA-06-D-6199 was not having valid permit and FC at the time of accident.

In support of that contention the learned counsel for 2 nd respondent has relied on the judgment of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in MFA No.967/2017 (MV-D) between Sri Venkatesh Vs. IFFCO TOKIO Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., and another.

sentences.text: This tribunal has carefully perused the Division Bench judgment relied from the side of 2nd respondent wherein, the Hon'ble Division Bench of our Hon'ble High court of Karnataka dismissed the MFA filed by the owner of the offending vehicle.
Further, the Hon'ble Division Bench observed that, the tribunal has rightly absolved the insurer and directed the owner of the vehicle to satisfy the award.
However, the judgment relied by the petitioner is a judgment of three bench.

The Hon'ble Apex Court held at para 15, "The appeal however would succeed to the limited extent that the amount of compensation determined by the High Court shall be first paid by respondent No.1 insurance company with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle (respondent No.2 herein)''.

Further the Hon'ble Apex Court held at para 17 that, "the appeals are partly allowed by directing respondent No.1 insurance company to first pay the compensation amount to the respective claimants as determined by the High Court and tribunal as the case may be, with liberty to recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle, respondent No.2''.
21.
In the said case also, the defence of the insurance company was that the offending vehicle had not possessed valid permit.
In the instant case also the contention of 2 nd respondent is that the offending vehicle had no valid permit,
However, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that clarifies the responsibility of an insurance company to pay compensation in a motor accident case where the offending vehicle lacked a valid permit.

The Supreme Court held that even if the insurance company has a right to recover the amount paid from the owner due to the violation of policy conditions (like the lack of a valid permit), the initial liability to pay the compensation to the victim falls on the insurance company.
This "pay and recover" principle ensures that victims are not denied compensation due to disputes between the owner and the insurer.
Therefore, the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court is aptly applicable to the case on hand.

22. By relying on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court referred to above, the 2nd respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization and further the 2 nd respondent-insurer is at liberty to recover the award amount from the 1 st respondent - R.C. owner of the offending vehicle in accordance with law.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the partly Affirmative.
23. ISSUE No.3:- In view of discussion made above, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following.

:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.
 Petitioners are awarded just and  reasonable compensation of Rs.17,16,715/- (Rupees Seventeen lakhs sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifteen Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.

On deposit of compensation amount, Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are entitled for 50% each with interest.
with interest is to be paid to them through E-payment on proper identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court and remaining 50% of their share with interest shall be invested in F.D. in their respective names in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years.

The petitioners have lost their son at their young age.
In the instant case both petitioners are the parents of the deceased minor.
By applying the said table to the present facts of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,16,715/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
18.
Driving License:- The 2nd respondent has contended that, the driver of offending Bus bearing Reg.No. KA-06-D-6199 was not holding valid driving license at the time of accident, but it has not produced the documents in order to prove the same.
Charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that the driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.
Therefore,
it appears to this Tribunal that, the driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid D.L. to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Insurance Policy, liability and Interest:-
In the instant case, respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-D-6199 and it was in force as on the date of accident.
The same was subject to the terms and conditions.
The Supreme Court held that even if the insurance company has a right to recover the amount paid from the owner due to the violation of policy conditions (like the lack of a valid permit), the initial liability to pay the compensation to the victim falls on the insurance company.
This "pay and recover" principle ensures that victims are not denied compensation due to disputes between the owner and the insurer.
